correctness.rationale: For two conjugate binary-input experiments and equal prior, set M=(P+Q)/2, Z=(P−Q)/(P+Q) on M-positive symbols (centered and |Z|≤1). Tagged pooling gives Δ=1/2[I(H;A,A′)−I(H;A,B)]=1/2 E[h(−ZZ′)−h(ZZ′)], where h(t)=(1+t)log(1+t) and Z,Z′ iid. Expand h(t)=t+Σ_{n≥2}(−1)^n t^n/[n(n−1)], which converges absolutely uniformly on [−1,1], and use EZ=0: Δ=Σ_{j≥1}(E Z^{2j+1})²/[(2j)(2j+1)]≥0. All vanish iff every odd moment vanishes, hence the law of Z is symmetric by polynomial density on [−1,1]. For two letters and P≠Q, symmetry iff P(0)+Q(0)=1; for weak contrast first coefficient ε^6 (E_M u³)^2/6; example exactly log(4096/3125)/16. Independent direct tensor JS confirms 0.01691103778430264 and positive sign; 1500-term series partial sum differs by ~1.04e−5 because endpoint |Z|=1 and is NOT an infinite numerical proof.
